ExplanationParts.CorpusEarnedOpening: One hall address places “bronze-headed and iron-browed” directly under “the patch-robed monk's gate.” Verses nevertheless say that even such a fellow receives a welt from one staff-blow, or stands bloodied under the staff's command.
EvidenceBody: Elsewhere the phrase itself answers “What is buddha?”, followed by the equally concrete “bird's beak and fish's gills.” These occurrences establish the epithet and its Chan setting; they do not establish literal metal anatomy or an occult quality. The headword occurs 208 times across 114 allowlisted texts.
